model_guidance:
TEST-STANDARD RECONCILIATION (critical — do this before comparing tables): German figures (Jentz/Panzerbeschusstafeln, reproduced at panzerworld.com/armor-penetration-table) = 50% probability of COMPLETE penetration ('durchschlagend') vs homogeneous rolled plate ~220-265 BHN at 30 deg from vertical. Soviet firing-table figures = DeMarre-computed with K=2400, two limits: PTP 'initial' (back-surface intact limit) and PSP 'certified/guaranteed' (>=75-80% of shell mass passes); republished single-column Soviet values (GvA, battlefield.ru) are the certified ones and run ~10-15% LOW vs the German 50% criterion for identical performance (tankarchives 'KwK 43 vs D-25T': D-25 re-rated to US 50% criterion = 196/179/158/125 mm @100/500/1000/2000 vs Soviet-table 150/143/126/97). Engine rule: pick ONE internal criterion (recommend 50%); multiply Soviet-table pens by 1.10-1.15 when mixing with German-table pens.

DeMARRE (range/velocity interpolation and new-shell synthesis): V = K * d^0.75 * b^0.7 / sqrt(m), with d=caliber(dm), b=plate(dm), m=mass(kg), V=m/s. Invert: b_mm = 100 * (V*sqrt(m)/(K*d^0.75))^(1/0.7). K=2400 (Soviet standard, medium-hardness RHA, blunt APBC); K~=2600 for post-war/US-criterion match; K~=2200 for uncapped sharp AP vs high-hardness plate. Fixed-shell scaling: Pen ∝ V^1.43. Get V(range) either from published tables or exponential decay V(x)=V0*exp(-c*x): fit c from any two table points; typical c: full-caliber APCBC 7.5-8.8cm ~ (0.9-1.1)e-4 per m; APCR ~ (2.5-3.5)e-4 per m (PzGr.40 sheds ~130-150 m/s per 500 m vs ~55-65 for PzGr.39); Soviet 76mm APHEBC ~1.3e-4.

SLOPE EFFECT (Bird & Livingston, 'WWII Ballistics: Armor and Gunnery', Overmatch Press 2001 — the reference every serious modeler uses): effective resistance = T * M(theta, T/d), NOT plain LOS. M depends on ammo nose type and overmatch T/d. Anchors at T/d=1, APCBC: 15deg:1.04, 30deg:1.20-1.25, 45deg:1.60-1.70, 55deg:2.10-2.20, 60deg:2.50 (rising to ~2.9 at T/d 1.2-1.5). B&L worked example (verified via forum reproductions): 75mm APCBC vs 45mm@60deg (T-34 glacis, T/d=0.6) -> M=2.7 -> 122mm RHA-equivalent. Overmatch dependence: M = M1(theta)*(T/d)^k(theta), k~0.03 at 30deg growing to ~0.15-0.3 at 60deg (heavily overmatched plates trend toward pure LOS). Blunt-nosed Soviet APBC (BR-350A/B, BR-365, BR-412B, BR-471B) has FLATTER slope curves: 60deg M~1.8-2.2 (their design goal vs German slopes); uncapped sharp AP worst full-caliber: 60deg M~3.0+; APCR (WWII carrier type): 30deg ~1.35, 45deg ~2.0, 60deg ~3.5-5.0. Cheap closed form valid 0-60deg: M=1/cos^n(theta), n=1.1-1.2 blunt APBC, 1.3-1.4 APCBC, 1.6-1.9 APCR, ~2.0 for shatter-prone uncapped AP. NORMALIZATION: only apply (+4 to +5 deg effective, WoT-style) below ~45 deg for capped shells if you insist on LOS models; B&L data shows ANTI-normalization beyond 45 deg — never let normalization reduce a 60deg T-34 glacis below the M values above. RICOCHET: full-caliber AP/APC auto-ricochet threshold ~>68-70 deg impact (roll d100 rising from 55 deg), APCR ~>65 deg, blunt APBC most ricochet-resistant (~>72 deg); HE fuzes regardless.

FACE-HARDENED PLATE + SHATTER GAP (B&L ch. on shatter; GvA 'Face Hardened Armour' page): German FH limited to <=50-55mm plates (Pz III/IV fronts). Vs capped German-style APC/APCBC: FH ~0.90-0.96 x RHA. Vs uncapped/poorly-capped Soviet AP: +10-30% effective when T/d>=0.8 (nose shatter); this is why 45mm and BR-350A failed vs Pz III 50mm. Blunt APBC partially immune to FH (blunt nose doesn't shatter): treat FH ~1.0 x RHA vs BR-350B/BR-365. SHATTER-GAP rule (famous for US 76mm M62, applies to BR-350A class): if shell cap quality is 'soft' AND target is FH or >=400 BHN AND impact velocity is 1.05-1.25 x ballistic-limit velocity AND T/d in 0.8-1.3 -> shell shatters: penetration x0.70-0.85 in exactly that velocity window (i.e., can fail point-blank yet penetrate at 500-800 m). Soviet 8S high-hardness plate (T-34, SU-100, ~400-450 BHN): +5-10% vs undermatching shot, but brittle: when overmatched (d/T>=1.5, e.g. 88mm vs 45mm) reduce required pen ~15% ((T/d)^0.15 style) AND on ANY solid frontal 88 hit spawn internal spall even without full penetration (NII-48/Aberdeen: 88 PzGr.39 cracked T-34 glacis outright). CAST: 0.95 x RHA thin, 0.85 x RHA >150mm sections (IS turrets). Late-war German plate (Tiger II, some Panther G): 0.85-0.95 + elevated spall.

RESIDUAL VELOCITY (Lambert-Jonas, standard in the literature; Recht-Ipson equally accurate per Segletes): Vr = a * (Vs^p - Vbl^p)^(1/p) for Vs>Vbl else 0. Lambert 1978 fit: p = 2 + z/3 with z = (T/d)*sec(theta) (LOS thickness in calibers); a = m/(m+m_plug) ~ 0.92-1.0 full-caliber AP (use a=0.95, p=2 as cheap default). Vbl = velocity where your pen model equals T*M (invert DeMarre). BEHIND-ARMOR: German PzGr.39 APHE with Bd.Z.5127 delay fuze bursts 1.2-1.5 m inside — model as fragmentation burst of filler_g + shell body (near-guaranteed crew/ammo kill in T-34 volume); fuze needs ~15-20mm plate to arm (over-penetration through thin skirts = reduced effect). Soviet APHE (MD-5/MD-8) same pattern, bigger fillers. Solid shot/APCR: damage = spall cone half-angle 15-20 deg about exit normal, energy budget 0.5*m_r*Vr^2 split ~60% shot body / 40% plate spall at T/d~1 (scale spall share with T/d); APCR spawns ~50% of full-caliber spall (core-only). Crew-kill scaling: fragment lethal if >2-5 kJ. HE vs armor (non-penetrating): 122mm OF-471 (3.6 kg TNT) and 152mm OF-530/OF-540 (5.9-6.9 kg) defeat plates <= ~caliber/2 by scabbing/weld rupture — trigger internal spall event + module (track/engine/turret-ring) damage on any hit; 152mm turret hits historically tore turrets off (model overpressure kill if plate <=75mm).

ARMOR SOURCES: German layouts per Jentz/Doyle Panzer Tracts + Spielberger; Soviet per NII-48 schemes as republished (Baryatinsky, tankarchives, tanks-encyclopedia). Gun sources per shell in each entry. Biggest unresolved conflicts flagged inline: (1) BR-365P MV 1020-1050 vs GvA 1200 (use 1050); (2) BR-412 filler 61 g vs 600 g; (3) L/43-vs-L/48 rows for 7.5cm KwK 40; (4) Soviet 30-deg rows for 76.2mm/152mm derived x0.8 from 0-deg, not archive-verified; (5) IS-2 m.1944 glacis cast 120 vs rolled 90-100 (both real, by factory).
